L173: # Token Broker Specification
L174: 
L175: # Token Broker Specification
L176: 
L177: 【110†Section titled “Token Broker Specification”】
L178: 
L179: Version: 1.0.0
L180: Status: Experimental draft
L181: Date: 2026-10-30
L182: Editors: GitHub Agentic Workflows maintainers
L183: Latest version: 【44†Token Broker Specification】
L184: ## Abstract
L185: 
L186: 【75†Section titled “Abstract”】
L187: This specification defines a deployment-owned HTTPS service that exchanges a verified GitHub Actions OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity token for a short-lived credential. Two independent capabilities authorize GitHub Copilot inference requests and Copilot coding-agent task operations. The specification defines the wire contract, issuer verification, tenant and workflow authorization, credential issuance, renewal, failure handling, and compliance tests.
L188: It does not define a public GitHub credential-minting API or supply a server implementation.
L189: ## Status of This Document
L190: 
L191: 【76†Section titled “Status of This Document”】
L192: 
L193: Token broker authentication is experimental. The protocol, configuration, and behavior may change without deprecation. Compiling a workflow that enables either broker capability emits an experimental-feature warning.
L194: This is a project specification following W3C-style conventions, not a W3C Recommendation. Repository maintainers govern changes through the normal contribution and review process. Version numbers follow semantic versioning: incompatible contract changes increment the major version, backward-compatible features increment the minor version, and clarifications increment the patch version.
L195: Implementation status (informative): Partial integration. The shared client supports both token types. Coding-agent task creation and issue-assignment integrations obtain credentials at request time and renew them as necessary. Brokered Copilot inference is wired for the bounded detection and evals jobs. Main-agent inference remains blocked on a renewable AWF credential provider.
L196: The compiler rejects broker-enabled GitHub-backed inference in the main agent job, including applicable fallback models; this is not limited to the engine named `copilot`. A successful standalone `copilot-request` exchange does not establish working cloud inference. Full end-to-end acceptance has not been achieved. Server implementation, deployment, and issuer integrations remain deployment-owned.

L212: ## 1. Introduction
L213: 
L214: 【78†Section titled “1. Introduction”】
L215: ### 1.1. Purpose and scope
L216: 
L217: 【79†Section titled “1.1. Purpose and scope”】
L218: 
L219: The broker removes the need to distribute long-lived capability credentials to participating workflows. It accepts a GitHub-signed job identity, applies deployment policy, and returns only a credential and its expiration.
L220: A capability is an operation class identified by `token_type`. A tenant is a deployment-enrolled security boundary bound to stable GitHub owner and repository identities. An execution context identifies a repository, workflow, run, attempt, and credential-consuming job. An issuer adapter is a trusted server component that obtains a credential from an approved backend.
L221: This specification covers broker exchange and its compiler/client integration contract. It does not cover admission decisions, billing, arbitrary GitHub authentication, provider endpoint discovery, deployment provisioning, or a new secret store. The 【43†admission service】 remains independent.
L222: ### 1.2. Design goals (informative)
L223: 
L224: 【80†Section titled “1.2. Design goals (informative)”】
L225: 
L226: The protocol deliberately excludes caller-selected scopes, tenant IDs, resource URLs, and provider endpoints. The server derives authority from verified identity and enrolled policy, not from caller assertions. Capabilities remain independent so that a deployment can enable only the operations it can securely issue.
L227: 
L228: ## 2. Conformance
L229: 
L230: 【81†Section titled “2. Conformance”】
L231: ### 2.1. Requirements notation
L232: 
L233: 【82†Section titled “2.1. Requirements notation”】
L234: 
L235: The key words “MUST”, “MUST NOT”, “REQUIRED”, “SHALL”, “SHALL NOT”, “SHOULD”, “SHOULD NOT”, “RECOMMENDED”, “NOT RECOMMENDED”, “MAY”, and “OPTIONAL” in this document are to be interpreted as described in 【111†RFC 2119†www.ietf.org】.
L236: Sections 2–7 and Appendix C are normative except where explicitly marked informative. The introduction, implementation status, examples, references, deployment decisions, and change log are informative. Requirements apply to the named actor; a server-only implementer is not responsible for implementing the compiler.
L237: ### 2.2. Conformance classes
L238: 
L239: 【83†Section titled “2.2. Conformance classes”】
L240: Class  | Requirements
L241: --- | ---
L242: Broker server  | Satisfies all server requirements, including rejection and isolation requirements, for its declared capability set.
L243: Compiler and runtime client  | Satisfies configuration, transport, response-validation, caching, and credential-handling requirements.
L244: Integrated deployment  | Combines conforming components and demonstrates actual downstream use and renewal for each claimed capability.
L245: A broker MUST declare its supported capability set to operators. The set MAY contain either capability, both, or neither. An empty set can conform to the exchange and rejection protocol but cannot claim usable credential issuance. Omission of an optional capability is not partial conformance. An implementation failing a mandatory requirement MUST NOT claim conformance.
L246: These are role-based classes, not escalating Basic/Standard/Complete levels. Inference and task support are independent, not tiers. Conformance claims MUST identify the specification version, class, supported capabilities, and test results. Client unit tests alone MUST NOT be presented as server or integrated-deployment certification.
L247: ## 3. Runtime Configuration and Trust Boundaries
L248: 
L249: 【84†Section titled “3. Runtime Configuration and Trust Boundaries”】
L250: 
L251: Workflow source MUST explicitly select one or both capabilities using `token-broker.copilot-request: true` and/or `token-broker.copilot-task: true`. Omission MUST preserve existing authentication. An inherited broker URL alone MUST NOT enable workflow-handler broker authentication. `copilot-request` MUST NOT be combined with `permissions.copilot-requests: write`.

L42: # The Action Evidence Boundary for Consequential Agent Effects
L43: ## 【21†Abstract】
L44: 
L45: Consequential agent actions can cross identity, transport, authorization, policy, and execution systems. Each system can produce a valid artifact while the executor still lacks a safe rule for joining the artifacts to the exact effect, consuming one-time authority, and handling an uncertain outcome. This document defines the Action Evidence Boundary (AEB), an executor-side processing model for that lifecycle.【22†¶】
L46: AEB requires native artifact verification, Canonical Action Identifier (CAID) matching, Authorization Evidence Chain (AEC) satisfaction, a separate local authorization decision, durable atomic consumption or reservation, invocation, closed effect outcomes, and authenticated reconciliation. It defines no receipt or token format, no policy language, no universal evidence taxonomy, and no new registry.
L47: Native workload credentials, message signatures, attested per-action tokens, permit records, authorization receipts, and status mechanisms retain their own semantics and verifiers.【23†¶】

L141: ## 【36†1.】 【37†Introduction】
L142: 
L143: A remote executor can receive several independently useful inputs: a workload credential and protected request, a delegation or capability, a pre-execution permit, a human-authorization artifact, and a policy decision. None of those inputs alone answers every question the consequence-owning system has to answer before changing its system of record.【117†¶】
L144: The missing contract is at the effect boundary. The executor must determine what exact material action it is about to perform; verify each artifact under its native rules; correlate independently verified representations without guessing; evaluate whether the evidence bundle fills its requirement; make its own authorization decision; consume or reserve any one-time or bounded authority; invoke the effect once; and preserve uncertainty when the effect cannot be observed conclusively.【118†¶】
L145: This document defines that contract. Its required order is:【119†¶】
L146: 
L147:      native verification
L148:             |
L149:             v
L150:      CAID material-action MATCH
L151:             |
L152:             v
L153:      AEC evidence SATISFIED
L154:             |
L155:             v
L156:      local policy AUTHORIZED
L157:             |
L158:             v
L159:      atomic CONSUMED / RESERVED
L160:             |
L161:             v
L162:      durable DISPATCH_PENDING
L163:             |
L164:             v
L165:      INVOKED
L166:             |
L167:             +--> EXECUTED
L168:             +--> FAILED
L169:             +--> INDETERMINATE --> authenticated reconciliation
L170: 【120†¶】
L171: 
L172: Every arrow is conditional. A signature is not authority. Native verification is not action correlation. Action correlation is not evidence satisfaction. Evidence satisfaction is not local authorization. Authorization is not execution. An invocation error is not proof that no effect occurred.【121†¶】
L173: ### 【38†1.1.】 【39†Scope and Non-Goals】
L174: 
L175: AEB specifies processing requirements for a boundary that controls a consequential effect. It can be implemented at a protocol gateway, service mesh component, application middleware, execution adapter, or system-of-record write path, provided the deployment states which effect paths the boundary actually mediates.【122†¶】
L176: 
L177: AEB does not define:【123†¶】
L178:   * a new authorization receipt, access token, attestation token, permit, credential, or execution-evidence format;【124†¶】
L179:   * a native signature, credential, revocation, status, or transparency verification algorithm;【125†¶】
L180:   * a policy language, universal authorization decision, or universal human-approval inference;【126†¶】
L181:   * general semantic equivalence between actions;【127†¶】
L182:   * provider truth, physical truth, legality, safety, wisdom, or complete mediation merely because an AEB implementation is present; or【128†¶】
L183:   * a registry for evidence types, states, action mappings, or verifier names.【129†¶】
L184: ## 【40†2.】 【41†Conventions and Terminology】
L185: 
L186: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [【130†RFC2119】] [【131†RFC8174】] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.【132†¶】
L187: 
L188: BCP 14 is indexed by the RFC Editor at [【133†BCP14】].【134†¶】
L189: Effect boundary:
L190:     The last control point that can withhold the protected mutation before it is submitted to the effecting system.【135†¶】
L191: 
L192: Relying party:
L193:     The party that selects trust inputs, action definitions, mapping profiles, evidence requirements, freshness rules, and local authorization policy, and that relies on the resulting decision.【136†¶】
L194: 
L195: Native artifact:
L196:     An evidence, credential, permit, token, receipt, status, or message-protection object defined outside AEB and verified under its own specification.【137†¶】
L197: 
L198: Field-origin assertion:
L199:     A native artifact in which an issuer asserts how exact fields of an action representation were sourced or transformed, and optionally the point-in-time snapshot on which that assertion rests. Verification establishes the issuer's signed assertion under pinned trust inputs; it does not independently establish where the bytes truly originated.【138†¶】
L200: 
L201: Observed action:
L202:     The immutable material action constructed by the effect boundary from executor-controlled parsing and system-of-record facts.【139†¶】
L203: 
L204: Material field:
L205:     A field whose change can alter the protected consequence, as declared by the selected CAID action-type definition.【140†¶】
L206: 
L207: Invocation:
L208:     The first dispatch of the frozen authorized action to a component that can cause the protected effect.【141†¶】
L209: 
L210: Authoritative reconciliation:
L211:     An authenticated, audience-bound observation from the effecting provider or system of record that is matched to the original action and operation identifier.【142†¶】
L212: ## 【42†3.】 【43†Non-Collapsing Decision and Lifecycle Vocabulary】
L213: 
L214: AEB uses the following decisions with the meanings established by the EMILIA architecture and its component drafts:【143†¶】
L215: VERIFIED:
L216:     One native artifact passed its native verifier under relying-party-selected trust inputs.【144†¶】
L217: 
L218: MATCH:
L219:     Independently verified artifacts denote the same material action directly or under exact relying-party-pinned CAID mapping profiles.【145†¶】
L220: 
L221: SATISFIED:
L222:     Verified and matched evidence fills every slot in the relying party's AEC requirement.【146†¶】
L223: 
L224: AUTHORIZED:
L225:     The consequence-owning relying party's local policy permits this exact action at this time.【147†¶】
L226: EXECUTED:
L227:     The executor records, or an accepted native artifact attests, that the exact effect occurred. This meaning remains bounded by the native source and its trust assumptions.【148†¶】
L228: AEB also names operational lifecycle states:【149†¶】
L229: CONSUMED:
L230:     A one-time authorization, challenge, operation key, or equivalent native replay unit has been durably made unavailable for another invocation.【150†¶】
L231: 
L232: RESERVED:
L233:     Bounded state, such as a capability budget, has been durably fenced for the exact operation before invocation.【151†¶】
L234: 
L235: DISPATCH_PENDING:
L236:     A durable intent record binds the frozen action, operation identifier, provider environment, and reservation before any effecting dispatch can occur. Recovery treats a stranded intent as uncertain, not as unused authority.【152†¶】
L237: 
L238: INVOKED:
L239:     The protected effect was dispatched using the frozen authorized action and operation identifier.【153†¶】
L240: 
L241: FAILED:
